title: Spec → Plan → Implementation
trigger: The request is vague or multi-step.
goal: Drill a vague request into an approved spec, then a plan whose every task carries its own verification command, so nothing gets built on a guess.
verification: The human's explicit yes on the restated spec is recorded, every plan task names its verification command and expected pass signal, and each completed task reports the command's actual output.

title: Parallel Agent Development
trigger: Multiple independent tasks can run at once.
goal: Run agents in parallel on measured, disjoint file sets with one lead owning shared files and integration, accepting work only from what is on disk.
verification: Each worker's git diff --name-only is a subset of its measured edit list, no two edit lists intersect, shared files were written only by the lead after the wave, and the full check passed on the integrated tree with the exit code read directly.

title: Root-Cause Debugging
trigger: A bug is unclear or recurring.
goal: Reproduce, isolate, fix, and verify root cause.
verification: The bug is reproduced on demand before any fix lands, the named root cause explains every observed symptom, and the reproduction plus a new regression test fail on the old code and pass on the fixed code.

title: Fresh-Context Code Review
trigger: Before merging or trusting agent-authored code.
goal: Get one independent review from a reviewer that never saw the author's reasoning, re-runs the evidence itself and ends with file:line findings and a verdict.
verification: A reviewer given none of the author's context or summary re-ran the checks itself, recorded exit codes and pass/skip/fail counts against a baseline, and returned file:line findings with an explicit APPROVE or CHANGES REQUESTED verdict.

title: Security Review Sprint
trigger: Code touches auth, secrets, network, parsers, permissions, or public release.
goal: Find reachable issues with evidence and false-positive notes.
verification: Every reported finding names its reachable entry point with the input or code path that reaches it, every dismissed alert carries a written false-positive reason, each fix ships with a test that fails on the vulnerable code, and the report contains no secret values and no probing outside the authorized scope.

title: Browser Runtime QA
trigger: A browser app, page, or automation flow needs validation.
goal: Verify real runtime behavior, console, network, and accessibility where relevant.
verification: Each tested flow has a screenshot of its final state, a console log with no unexplained errors and a network capture with no unexplained failed requests, and every bug found comes with numbered reproduction steps that a second run followed to the same result, with no payment, permission or secret prompt clicked without approval.

title: Release Runbook
trigger: A change is ready to publish, deploy, or announce.
goal: Stage rollout with readiness evidence and rollback criteria.
verification: The released version or build hash is read back from the target environment, the first-hour checks are recorded against their thresholds, and the rollback trigger is written down with a rollback path that was dry-run before the rollout started.

title: Research Brief
trigger: A decision depends on current facts or external sources.
goal: Produce a brief where every finding has a source actually read, a mechanism and a confidence label, with the search filter's blind spots named and a skeptic pass done.
verification: Every finding cites a source that was actually read, states its mechanism and confidence, and survived a fresh-context skeptic pass on the raw material, with the expectation dated before the first search result.

title: Local AI Stack Setup
trigger: A local or self-hosted AI stack is needed.
goal: Install and verify a private/local agent stack safely.
verification: From a fresh shell the health check reports ready and every model in the runtime matrix answers a test prompt with its runtime version and hardware recorded, the rollback path has been exercised once, and a scan of the setup notes and logs finds no tokens.

title: Repo Growth Launch
trigger: A public repository needs useful packaging and launch readiness.
goal: Launch a public repo honestly: content that survives a click-through, one rule-following submission per venue, fast replies to contributors, and every public action by the maintainer.
verification: A 14-day traffic baseline is recorded, the content audit shows no templated files in what is promoted, a venue table links each venue's rules, and the launch log shows every post was made by the maintainer.

title: Change Impact Map
trigger: Before an agent edits unfamiliar code or a risky area.
goal: Map the blast radius before implementation starts.
verification: Before the first edit, a written map lists every file, caller, consumer and test the change can reach, each entry backed by the search or call-graph command that found it, and the final diff stays inside that map or each extra file carries the human's approval.

title: Agent Task Contract and Scope Box
trigger: Before delegating a task to an AI agent.
goal: Give the agent a brief it can execute alone: one outcome, a measured edit list, forbidden actions, earlier lessons, a done condition that is a command, and a report checkable on disk.
verification: The returned git diff --name-only is a subset of the measured edit list, every unchanged edit-list file is explained, the lead reran the stated verification command and read its exit code directly, and new friction was appended to the lessons file.

title: Regression-Test-First Bug Fix
trigger: A bug has a concrete symptom or user report.
goal: Capture the bug as a test that goes red on the exact symptom, green after the fix and red again when the fix is removed, with the cause marked measured or inferred.
verification: A test reproducing the reported symptom went red on the unfixed code, green after the fix and red again when the fix was deliberately undone, with suite pass/skip/fail counts unchanged apart from the new test.

title: Minimized Reproducer Factory
trigger: A bug is vague, flaky, environment-specific, or reported only in logs.
goal: Turn a symptom into the smallest runnable reproduction.
verification: A single self-contained script or test, runnable from a clean checkout without new heavyweight dependencies or services, fails with the same error signature as the original report on every run, and each input or line removed during minimization was shown not to be needed.

title: Golden Master Refactor
trigger: Refactoring legacy or under-tested code where behavior must stay stable.
goal: Lock current behavior with characterization tests before changing structure.
verification: Characterization tests recorded against the pre-refactor code pass unchanged against the refactored code, the tests were shown to catch a deliberately injected behavior change, and any golden output that changed has the human's sign-off as an intended fix rather than a regression.

title: Agent Patch Intake Triage
trigger: An agent returns a diff, branch, patch, or pull request.
goal: Separate useful changes from scope creep before deeper review.
verification: Every hunk of the returned diff is classified as in scope, scope creep or noise against the original task, the accepted subset applies cleanly and passes the task's tests, and each rejected or deferred hunk is listed with the human's decision recorded.

title: Review Feedback Application Loop
trigger: A reviewer left comments on an agent-authored PR.
goal: Classify feedback, apply minimal fixes, and verify each resolved thread.
verification: Each reviewer thread maps to a commit that addresses it or a written reply explaining why not, the tests covering each fix pass, the diff changes no behavior beyond what the comments asked for, and the reviewer has resolved every thread, including any comment that was declined.

title: API Contract Change Lockstep
trigger: Changing public APIs, schemas, events, CLI flags, or config formats.
goal: Update producers, consumers, docs, fixtures, and contract tests together.
verification: One change set updates the schema together with every producer and consumer found by search, the docs and the fixtures, the contract tests pass on both sides of the boundary, and any breaking change carries a human-approved deprecation note and migration date.

title: CI Red-to-Green Reproducer
trigger: CI fails after an agent change.
goal: Reproduce the failing item alone with its full output and real exit code, name the failed component, fix the cause and show counts matching the baseline.
verification: The single failing item was re-run alone with the check's exact command, its real exit code and stdout/stderr identified the failing component (cause marked measured or inferred), and after the fix the pass/skip/fail counts match the baseline.

title: Flaky Test Burn-Down
trigger: A test passes on rerun but fails intermittently.
goal: Capture nondeterminism and fix the root cause instead of rerunning to green.
verification: The flake is first made to fail on demand by pinning the seed, ordering or timing, the named root cause is fixed, and the test then passes a stated number of consecutive isolated reruns with the rerun log attached and no skip, retry or timeout added without human approval.

title: Dependency Upgrade Shepherd
trigger: Bumping libraries, frameworks, runtimes, lockfiles, or build tools.
goal: Upgrade with changelog context, tests, and rollback notes.
verification: The lockfile diff shows only the intended bumps plus explained transitive changes, the build and full test suite pass on the new versions, every breaking change in the changelog between the old and new versions is mapped to a code change or marked not applicable, and the rollback note names the exact prior versions to restore.

title: Urgent Hotfix Fast Path
trigger: A production-impacting regression needs a fast patch.
goal: Constrain work to reproduce, fix, smoke, and decide rollback or roll-forward.
verification: The production symptom is reproduced before the patch and absent after it in a smoke test against the target environment, the diff contains only the fix, and the rollback or roll-forward decision is recorded with the approving human's name and time.

title: Incident Command Center
trigger: A pager alert, customer-impacting incident, or severe degradation is active.
goal: Assemble evidence, owners, mitigations, and status updates without letting the agent take unsafe action.
verification: A timestamped incident log links every status update and mitigation to the dashboard, query or log line behind it, every open action has a named owner, and every production change or outgoing message in the log shows the incident commander's approval before it was carried out.

title: Blameless Postmortem and Action Ledger
trigger: An incident is stabilized or closed.
goal: Produce an evidence-backed timeline, contributing factors, and follow-up ledger.
verification: Every timeline entry cites a timestamped log, alert, chat message or deploy record, contributing factors are written as system conditions with no individual blamed, and every follow-up in the ledger has an owner, a due date and a tracking issue that stakeholders approved.

title: Migration Readiness and Cutover Planner
trigger: A schema, API, platform, vendor, or data migration is proposed.
goal: Plan phases, dual-run checks, canaries, rollback, and go/no-go criteria.
verification: Each phase has measurable go or no-go criteria and a rollback trigger, the dual-run comparison shows the old and new systems agreeing on counts or outputs within a stated tolerance, the rollback was rehearsed outside production, and the cutover time and any irreversible step carry human sign-off.

title: Documentation Drift Audit
trigger: Docs may be stale after feature, process, or dependency changes.
goal: Compare docs against source behavior and fix contradictions with evidence.
verification: Every doc claim checked is listed with the source file, command or test that confirms or contradicts it, each contradiction is fixed in a diff that cites that evidence, and every corrected behavior claim carries the subject-matter owner's approval before publication.

title: ADR Decision Capture from Threads
trigger: A decision happened in chat, meeting notes, issue comments, or PR discussion.
goal: Convert messy discussion into context, options, decision, consequences, and owners.
verification: The ADR links or quotes the source thread for its context, options and decision, names an owner for each consequence, and carries an explicit approval from every decision participant before it is merged.

title: Role-Based Onboarding Trail
trigger: A new hire, transfer, contractor, or agent needs to ramp into a repo or system.
goal: Create a role-specific path with starter tasks and verification checkpoints.
verification: A newcomer in the target role completes the starter tasks using only the trail and passes each verification checkpoint, such as a local build, a passing test run and a first merged change, and the mentor has confirmed in writing that every task is safe for a newcomer.

title: Knowledge Transfer and Bus-Factor Reduction
trigger: A system depends on one person, a rotation is coming, or ownership is changing.
goal: Create ownership maps, runbooks, glossary, and a Q&A backlog.
verification: Someone other than the current owner carries out a critical procedure, such as a deploy or a restore, using only the written runbook, the ownership map names a backup for every critical path, and the current owner has validated the emergency steps.

title: Workflow Evaluation Harness
trigger: A new agent workflow, prompt, or automation needs repeatable quality checks.
goal: Define golden tasks, rubric, thresholds, and regression checks.
verification: Running the harness on the golden task set produces a scored report against the approved rubric and pass threshold, a repeat run reproduces the same scores, and a deliberately degraded version of the workflow falls below the threshold.

title: Prompt and Policy Change Control
trigger: Changing system prompts, guardrails, tool permissions, routing, or memory policy.
goal: Review intent, risk, before-after behavior, rollout, and rollback.
verification: The same eval set run before and after the change shows the intended behavior shift and no regression past the agreed threshold, rollback is a single revert to a recorded prior version, and the production rollout carries human approval of its privacy and security trade-offs.

title: Agent Memory Hygiene Review
trigger: Memory feels wrong, stale, conflicting, too full, or privacy-sensitive.
goal: Keep agent memory small, true as of today and lossless: free space by archiving full text with a pointer left behind, never by deleting, and make corrections visible.
verification: Index size is under budget, and every entry removed from the index is found verbatim in the archive by an archive search for a unique phrase, with a pointer line left behind.

title: Customer Signal to Roadmap Triage
trigger: Support tickets, interviews, reviews, sales notes, or churn reasons accumulate.
goal: Cluster evidence into themes, impact, and candidate roadmap items.
verification: Every theme links back to the specific tickets, interviews or notes that support it with a count, each candidate roadmap item cites its themes and an impact estimate, and PM, design and support have approved the prioritization before any commitment reaches users.

title: Multi-Repo Change Coordinator
trigger: A change spans multiple repositories, packages, services, docs, or deployment units.
goal: Sequence changes, compatibility shims, branch/PR mapping, and verification across repos.
verification: A table maps every affected repo to its branch, PR and merge position, each repo's tests pass against the new versions of the others, every compatibility shim is covered by a test of old against new, and the merge order carries human approval.

title: Git Worktree Agent Lanes
trigger: Multiple agents or humans need to work in the same repo concurrently.
goal: Give each agent its own worktree and branch cut from a fresh remote main, reaching main only through human-merged branches, never touching what another session owns.
verification: git worktree list shows the lane on its own branch cut from a freshly fetched origin/main, the shared checkout's HEAD and git status are unchanged, every lane commit holds only lane files, the branch is pushed, and the change was re-verified on the checkout that runs it after merge.

title: Context Compaction and Handoff
trigger: A long agent session is about to compact, hand off, or restart.
goal: Close a long session so the next one can continue from files alone: work pushed, branches tidy, lessons in memory, current state written as verified reality.
verification: Every touched repo shows zero unpushed commits against all remotes, the final hygiene check is clean or each open item is named, and each current-state line cites something run this session.

title: MCP and Tool Integration Review
trigger: Adding or changing an MCP server, tool, plugin, or external integration.
goal: Let nothing reach an agent until it passes a security scan, a human has read what it can execute and reach, and it fills a real gap; adopt only the smallest safe part.
verification: A saved pre-install scan report for the exact version adopted, every non-low finding triaged at file:line, a capability table, a fetched licence, and a recorded disposition (including skips) against an existing named capability.

title: Secrets and Config Audit
trigger: Before public release, CI setup, deployment, or repository handoff.
goal: Before a public push, prove the repo and its whole history carry no secrets, network details, personal data or process traces, and escalate what cannot be removed.
verification: Recorded scans over all refs and commit messages (secrets, IPv4/IPv6, hostnames, home paths, emails, names), run after checking file encodings, showing zero matches on the exact repo to be pushed, with any ever-committed secret rotated.

title: Agent-Written Docs Review
trigger: An agent produced README, API docs, changelog, tutorial, or launch copy.
goal: Check claims, dependency order, examples, and stale or exaggerated statements.
verification: Every factual claim in the doc is checked against code, a command run or a cited source and marked confirmed, corrected or removed, every example and install step was run in order from a clean environment, and claims about behavior, performance, security or roadmap carry the owner's approval.

title: Long-Running Task Checkpoint
trigger: A build, migration, scrape, benchmark, agent run, or batch job will run for a while.
goal: Run long jobs where the agent session cannot kill them, with logs that outlive it, a heartbeat, a clean stop and evidence of what was produced.
verification: The job's logs are readable after the launching session ends, heartbeats arrive at the expected interval, output counts taken inside the job match the expected or previous run, and stop exit codes are recorded.

title: Agent-Generated Test Review
trigger: An agent added tests, and coverage quality needs review before trusting the patch.
goal: Accept tests that protect real behavior and reject tests that only verify mocks, implementation details, or unproven assumptions.
verification: Each new test is shown failing against the unfixed code or a named mutation, its assertion checks user-visible behaviour, and the test command output is recorded.
